Commentary.Commentary: So West Indies will bat again, we have around 13 overs left today. Let's see how they bat this time. Stay tuned.
And here comes the confirmation - INDIA HAVE ENFORCED THE FOLLOW-ON!
India will be pretty happy with the 323-run lead but they could have folded the hosts much quicker than this.

Shami and Umesh Yadav finished with four wickets each as they bowled really well towards the end. Shami was better overall but Yadav was sensational in the final session. Ishant Sharma and Ravichandran Ashwin couldn't do much whereas Mishra struck twice.

Superb bowling performance by India! For West Indies, apart from Brathwaite and Dowrich, no batter got going. The opener played a gritty knock at the top but he didn't get any support from his teammates. The middle order crumbled as the Indian pacers made things difficult for the hosts. Dowrich impressed everyone with a fifty but unfortunately that wasn't enough.

Dowrich and Holder are batting currently but they have a mountain to climb as India are approaching to give a follow-on to the hosts. Let's see what happens in the final session. Can West Indies fight out hard and survive the last session? Or will India run through the tail and ask West Indies bat again? We'll come to know that in a short while, join us back to catch the action.

Yet another session that goes in India's favour. The visitors continue their domination in this Test match as West Indies are trailing by 409 runs and have just three wickets left in this innings. They lost four big wickets in this session as India bowled extremely well. Samuels and Blackwood got out in quick a succession as Shami bowled a terrific spell. Umesh Yadav joined the party as well later on as he removed Chase and Brathwaite who batted as a lone warrior. The opener was gritty but wasn't getting any support from his teammates.
FOUR! Cut away! Shorter in length, Dowrich gets back in his crease and cuts it through point for a superb boundery. Good way to end the session by West Indies. THAT'S TEA ON DAY 3.

...Day 3, second session...

Brathwaite has batted really well as he played sensibly and didn't go after the good balls. West Indies will depend on him and Samuels now else they could be in big trouble here. The hosts still trail by 476 runs and have a tough task ahead. Let's see how the Indian bowlers respond in the second session. Join us back in a bit to catch the action.

That's another good session for India! They got two wickets for 59 runs. Bishoo and Brathwaite started off cautiously early on as they were batting with a lot of grit. The Indian bowlers weren't really accurate with their line and length but Shami was looking dangerous. The speedster was awarded with the big wicket of Bravo after Mishra removed the nightwatchman Bishoo.

India will hope that their quickies improve their line and length and will want Ashwin to continue his heroics this time with the ball. Can West Indies fight back today? Or will India continue their dominance? Let's hope for another interesting and entertaining day of cricket.

Hello everyone to the coverage of the third day of the first Test between West Indies and India! Yesterday India put a big score on the board and asked West Indies to bat for the last few overs of the day and were successful to clinch their opening wicket towards the end of the day.
...Day 3, first session...

India have put a strong foothold over the match and would like to dismiss West Indies tomorrow itself and take a huge lead. On the other hand, Holder's men would look to fight out in the middle and will depend on the experience of Bravo and Samuels. So join us back tomorrow at 1930 IST to see the third day's proceedings. Till then, good bye and take care!

The Indian bowlers were pumped up but Ishant and Umesh did not actually bowl that well with the new ball. They were either too short or too full and though they did not spray the ball around, were not able to pick up wickets. The West Indian openers were just looking to see out the session. Afterwards, Shami and Ashwin looked dangerous towards the end and got the wicket of Chandrika in the penultimate over of the day, much to the disappointment of the Windies camp.

What a day it has been! Thoroughly dominated by India! Kohli made his maiden double century in Tests by leading the team from the front. Ashwin gave him strong support and then took the charge after the skipper's departure and made his third century against West Indies.The tailenders then took the aggressive route by taking the attack to the Carribean bowlers with Mishra making a quick half century.
